newsitem.title: POLAND: BPH, CS FIRST BOSTON IN EUROBOND DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BPH, CS FIRST BOSTON IN EUROBOND DEAL.

text.p: Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA (BPH) and CS First Boston Limited signed a letter of intent on Friday on the Polish bank's planned eurobond issue, BPH said in a statement.
It said BPH's general shareholders meeting would make a final decision on the issue. No further details were available and BPH officials were immediately available for comment.
BPH president Henryka Pieronkiewicz said in September the board would call an extraordinary shareholders meeting later this year to approve a convertible mark eurobond issue.

She also said BPH considered offering a part of the bond issue to a Polish bank undergoing privatisation in exchange for between 25 and 30 percent of the other bank's shares, but did not give the bank's name.
The next Polish bank to undergo privatisation is the Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA, slated for sale in April 1997. It has began building capital ties with PBR and Kredyt Bank .
Shareholders of the insurer Warta have approved a new share issue directed, among others, at BPH, Kredyt Bank and PBK, which Warta's spokesman said was aimed at creating a strong capital group.

The state has 46.6 percent of BPH. Among its other major shareholders are the Euroepan Bank for Reconstruction and Development with a 15.06 percent stake, and ING Barings and its subsidiary Bank Slaski with a joint 12.6 percent stake.
BPH, privatised in January 1995, is one of Poland's top 10 banks in terms of capital and assets.
